title: Energy in Chemical Reactions
seo_title: Reaction Energy Worksheets: Exothermic, Endothermic and Bond Energies (High School Chemistry)
standard_text: Develop a model to illustrate that the release or absorption of energy from a chemical reaction system depends upon the changes in total bond energy.
meta_desc: Free high school chemistry worksheets on energy in chemical reactions (NGSS HS-PS1-4): exothermic and endothermic reactions, bond energies, ΔH and energy diagrams. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: ΔH is the energy to break bonds minus the energy released forming new ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

ΔH = energy to break bonds − energy released forming bonds.

  • Breaking bonds absorbs energy; forming bonds releases energy.
  • More released than absorbed: exothermic, ΔH < 0 (surroundings get warmer). More absorbed: endothermic, ΔH > 0.
  • On an energy diagram, ΔH = products − reactants; activation energy = peak − reactants.
Example

H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl: broken 678 kJ, formed 862 kJ. ΔH?

678 − 862

Answer: −184 kJ (exothermic)

Example

Reactants 60 kJ, products 20 kJ, peak 90 kJ. Ea?

90 − 60

Answer: 30 kJ

Common mistakes

  • Thinking breaking bonds releases energy.
  • Thinking an exothermic reaction feels cold.
  • Reading the peak height as ΔH.

faq.q: How do you calculate ΔH from bond energies?
faq.a: Add the energies of all bonds broken in the reactants, then subtract the energies of all bonds formed in the products.

faq.q: How can you tell if a reaction is exothermic?
faq.a: It releases energy, so the surroundings get warmer and ΔH is negative. On a diagram, the products are lower than the reactants.
The energy needed to start a reaction: the peak of the energy diagram minus the energy of the reactants.

items.q: Ammonium nitrate dissolves and the water gets colder. What is the sign of ΔH for this change?
items.e: Energy released: ΔH < 0. Energy absorbed: ΔH > 0.

items.q: A hand warmer gets hot when opened. Is this exothermic or endothermic?
items.e: Exothermic releases energy (surroundings warm up); endothermic absorbs energy.

items.q: What is an endothermic reaction?
c: a reaction that absorbs energy from the surroundings

items.q: Plants use light energy to make glucose in photosynthesis. What is the sign of ΔH for this change?
items.e: Energy released: ΔH < 0. Energy absorbed: ΔH > 0.

items.q: Limestone (CaCO₃) must be heated strongly to make lime. What is the sign of ΔH for this change?
items.e: Energy released: ΔH < 0. Energy absorbed: ΔH > 0.

items.q: What is activation energy?
c: the energy needed to start a reaction

items.q: What is an exothermic reaction?
c: a reaction that only happens in cold places
